machine: Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S / XDNA2, 128 GB, Arch (Omarchy), Linux 7.2.15; power profile performance. Every run held the GPU and the NPU through the machine's scheduler (nobody else on them); other sessions' CPU work at a load average of 1-4.
software: llama.cpp b10944 Linux Vulkan release, Mesa 26.2.5 RADV, xrt 2.21.75; zest a87d2ae (before), and the commit this record comes with (results copied by the GPU; pieces with no multiply run by the GPU), then the one that turns the row split on by default

models.coder30: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct Q4_K_M: mixture of experts, width 2,048, 48 layers, 128 experts of 768, 8 used a token
models.dense: Qwen3.5-2B, Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B, all Q4_K_M

method: prefill bench at 2,048 tokens, -ngl 99 -n 0 -b 2048 -ub 2048 -r 3: median (min-max) of 3. Per-op GPU times from Vulkan's own timer (GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER=1, which waits for every op, so totals run longer than untimed runs): the second of two prompts.

gpu_alone_ms_per_prompt_coder30.reading: the multiplies zest can take (weights times activations) are 19% of the GPU's prompt; the expert step, which it cannot, 47%

the_expert_multiplies_after_a_zest_piece.what: ms per gate/up MUL_MAT_ID op (two a layer, the first ops to read the normed activations zest's second piece of a layer wrote), by how zest was run
the_expert_multiplies_after_a_zest_piece.zest_by_layer: bimodal: 4.5-5.0 in a quarter of the layers, 9-12.6 in the rest
the_expert_multiplies_after_a_zest_piece.other_ops_under_zest: attention 4.83 against 4.35 ms (its inputs q, 34 MB, and k and v, 4 MB each); the down multiplies and the rest unchanged
the_expert_multiplies_after_a_zest_piece.reading: zest wrote its results with ggml_backend_tensor_set, a memcpy into Vulkan's mapped memory. glibc's memcpy uses ordinary stores under 24 MB here (x86_non_temporal_threshold 0x1800000) and non-temporal ones from there; this model's results are 17 MB tensors. After an ordinary-store copy the GPU's next read of the tensor is slow. The GPU's clock is not it (sampled at 2 kHz it only follows how busy the GPU is), nor the host's threads.

prefill_tokens_s_pp2048.note: the three copy methods are one build with a switch (not kept): ggml's memcpy, a GPU copy from the piece's pinned memory, and that after flushing the source from the CPU's caches. The GPU alone was not rerun in that series; its figures are from ten minutes earlier.

npu_calls_of_an_experts_size_ms.method: the BFP16 kernel on 512 and 1,024 rows, median of 15, while another session's job had the GPU at 100% (so about a fifth slow)
npu_calls_of_an_experts_size_ms.reading: a pass of 512 (token, expert) rows through an expert costs about 0.66 ms, and a layer has 16,384 of them: 21 ms if every pass were full, against 12 ms for the GPU's expert step. The kernel also gives every column the same weights, so each expert (128 rows on average) would need its own passes. The NPU cannot take the expert step at a gain with this kernel.

prefill_tokens_s_pp2048.method: the same bench, n=3; each model's four figures within two minutes of each other

findings: On a mixture-of-experts model zest lost to the GPU alone (0.63x on the 30B, 0.51x on the 35B) for two reasons. More than half of the loss was not zest's own time: the GPU's expert multiplies ran at less than half speed after zest's pieces, because of how zest's results were copied into Vulkan's memory.

With the GPU doing that copy, zest reads the 30B at 0.84x the GPU alone (0.96x with the split at 50%) and the 35B at 0.79x at 08:45 and 0.92x at 09:42, when the GPU alone was itself slower on that model (0.92x and 1.05x with the split). Dense models gain 3-8%: the 27B without the split is at 340 against 344 for the GPU alone, and at 449 with it.

What is left is structure: the NPU can take a fifth of this model's work, in pieces of 4.5 ms that the GPU does in 2.4 ms, and at this width (2,048) the kernel's calls are about a millisecond, where its fixed costs show (15 TFLOPS against 25 on the 27B).
